query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: In an initially single-phase, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA), intermediate-temperature exposure (≈450–650 °C) enables short-range-order-driven diffusion that selectively enriches grain boundaries in Cr and Mn. The solute pile-up heterogeneously nucleates nano-scale, Cr-rich σ-phase platelets along the boundaries. The combined effect of (i) solute-induced reduction of grain-boundary cohesive energy and (ii) formation of hard, brittle intergranular σ precipitates lowers the local work-of-separation and changes the fracture mode from transgranular micro-void coalescence to intergranular quasi-cleavage, degrading room-temperature fracture toughness and impact energy by ≈40–60 % relative to the solution-annealed baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, single-phase FCC, grain size 5–20 µm, solution-annealed at 1100 °C/1 h and water-quenched; negligible pre-existing segregation or second phases.
generation.intervention: Isothermal aging at 550 °C for 100 h in high-vacuum or inert atmosphere (to avoid oxidation) followed by air cooling.
generation.conditions: Aging temperature window 450–650 °C; typical engineering strain rates (10⁻³–10⁻¹ s⁻¹) and test temperatures −196 °C to 300 K for toughness evaluation.
generation.structural_mediator: Cr- and Mn-enriched grain boundaries decorated with 5–20 nm Cr-rich σ-phase platelets at an area fraction ≥3 %.
generation.mechanism: Element-specific short-range ordering reduces diffusion barriers for Cr/Mn, driving their segregation to grain boundaries. The solute excess lowers boundary cohesive energy (adsorption-induced embrittlement). Concurrent σ-phase nucleation produces hard intergranular particles that act as crack-initiation sites and hinder dislocation transmission across boundaries, promoting intergranular fracture and brittle behavior.
generation.predicted_outcome: After aging, Charpy V-notch impact energy and J-integral fracture toughness at 298 K decrease by roughly 40–60 % (e.g., from ~200 kJ m⁻² to ≤120 kJ m⁻²); fracture surfaces show ≥70 % intergranular facets; nano-indentation across boundaries reveals a ≥20 % hardness jump at decorated boundaries.
generation.baseline: Solution-annealed material exhibits single-phase FCC, no detectable boundary segregation, fully transgranular ductile fracture, and high impact energy (~200 kJ m⁻²) and fracture toughness (K_IC ≈ 200 MPa·√m).
generation.boundary: Effect expected to saturate after ~100 h in 450–650 °C range; negligible below 400 °C (diffusion too slow) and reversed above 700 °C (precipitate dissolution). Persists under quasi-static and dynamic loading but diminishes at cryogenic temperatures where σ-phase is more ductile.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of segregation and σ-phase fraction may depend on trace impurities and exact thermal history; Mn volatility or competing carbide formation could suppress σ precipitation, moderating embrittlement.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two statistically identical CoCrFeMnNi HEA batches. Batch A: retain solution-annealed state. Batch B: age at 550 °C for 100 h in vacuum, then air-cool. Perform atom-probe tomography (APT) and high-resolution STEM on grain boundaries, measure Charpy V-notch impact energy and fracture toughness (J-integral or K_IC) at 298 K, and conduct fractography.
measurements: TEM/STEM imaging for σ-phase identification and size/area fraction
Fractography to quantify intergranular vs transgranular area fraction
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If aged Batch B either (a) shows <0.5 at.% Cr or Mn enrichment at grain boundaries, (b) shows no σ-phase precipitates >2 nm, or (c) retains ≥90 % of Batch A’s toughness with ≤10 % intergranular fracture, the hypothesis is falsified.
